checks.title: Active Sensing with Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Emitter Localization from RF Observations
checks.reading_scope: Selected passages from abstract p1, problem formulation p3, simulation and hyperparameters p4, evaluation VI(a,b) p5. Not a full independent reproduction.
checks.status: numeric claim verified; algorithm-selection extrapolation unsupported
findings: VI(a) reports PPO success 80.1 percent and DQN 76.3 percent.
The study uses a stationary GNSS source, multi-antenna IQ observations, Sionna indoor multipath simulation and navigation actions rather than bounded bearing multichannel complete clearing.
DQN and PPO use different gamma values and collection/update configurations; the percentage gap is not a controlled update-rule-only causal effect.
VI(b) recurrent PPO stability is supported mainly by value explained variance in Figure 7; do not convert this into directly measured accuracy of a certified belief.
The arXiv date is 2026, while the PDF carries a 2025 IEEE copyright line. Formal venue/date must be recorded separately rather than inferred.

checks.title: A Closer Look at Invalid Action Masking in Policy Gradient Algorithms
checks.reading_scope: Selected introduction and mechanism passages pp1-3, Proposition 1 proof p3, conclusion p6.
findings: State-dependent valid-action masking defines a differentiable behavior policy and Proposition 1 analyzes its policy gradient.
This result is not a theorem that candidate pruning preserves every optimal action, or that an exit mask guarantees finite complete clearing.
PPO likelihood ratios must refer to the same stored state/candidate payload/mask used during behavior sampling.

checks.title: Policy Invariance under Reward Transformations: Theory and Application to Reward Shaping
checks.reading_scope: Selected pp3-4: regularity/proper-policy assumptions, potential-difference form and Theorem 1 statement. Full proof and experiments not reread.
checks.status: classical result verified; task telescoping argument independently specified in PRE_REVIEW
findings: The paper states proper-policy assumptions for its undiscounted finite-state setup and boundedness qualifications for broader settings.
Potential shaping must use the same discount convention as the return; terminal and truncation handling cannot be omitted.
The task proposal still needs bounded potential, finite completion and an explicit T versus T/N objective; citing the theorem does not prove PPO convergence on compressed belief.

checks.title: OffRIPP: Offline RL-based Informative Path Planning
checks.reading_scope: Selected abstract p1, policy-learning Eq4-5 p3, datasets p4, TableI and comparison protocol p5, discussion p6. Not a reproduction.
checks.status: method identity verified; threshold explanation inconsistent; cross-task superiority unsupported
findings: Eq4 restricts actions by behavior probability greater than tau, while adjacent prose reverses the intuitive tau endpoints. With a strict greater-than gate, tau=1 can leave no actions.
A relative support gate with a nonempty fallback is a project-specific repaired definition; it must not be claimed as a byte-for-byte reproduction without reading official code.
TableI expert-data OffRIPP covariance traces23.28/7.83/3.96 are worse than generating behavior18.48/6.96/3.73. The paper explicitly does not treat that online-trained behavior as a matched baseline.
The table CAtNIPP comparison is naive offline PPO on a dataset, not the correctly online-trained PPO alternative proposed by A.
Reported benefit on particular light-intensity and fruit datasets supports investigating replay/support control, not a guarantee of improvement over strong C7 or PPO under the present cost objective.
